# Karltung efter budet på Bahnhof: ”Jag kan inte hålla på med det här för evigt"

**Feed**: dagen-med-di  
**Published**: 2026-08-18  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The episode is an interview with Bahnhof CEO Jon Karlung after Q2 results and Telenor's takeover bid. Q2 revenue was SEK 575m, up about 5%, with operating profit of SEK 71.6m. The company keeps its SEK 2.4bn full-year target, which implies nearly 10% growth in H2. Consumer customer growth is slowing because open city networks are a hard market. Growth in housing cooperatives, villas, enterprise connectivity and the Gothenburg bunker data centre project is presented as the offset. Karlung has agreed to sell his shares to Telenor at SEK 60 per share and does not expect the Swedish Competition Authority to demand concessions or block the deal. He argues Bahnhof's fixed-line strength and Telenor's mobile business complement each other rather than overlap.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟡 BAHN-B — Bahnhof | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Telenor bid at SEK 60/share is under competition review. The CEO has agreed to sell and expects approval. The business is stable and the FY target is kept.

#### Reasoning

The share price is effectively anchored to Telenor's SEK 60/share offer. CEO Jon Karlung (the guest, and a party to the deal) expects the Competition Authority to approve it without concessions because Bahnhof (fixed line) and Telenor (mobile) complement each other. The underlying business is stable: Q2 +5% growth, margins held, SEK 2.4bn target kept. The upside is capped at the bid, so holding until the deal closes is the implied position. This is not an explicit recommendation.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the Competition Authority blocks the deal or demands major concessions
- if Telenor withdraws or changes the SEK 60 bid
- if H2 growth falls well short of the ~10% needed for the SEK 2.4bn target

> *"Jag tror inte det, därför att det är ett stabilt... Vi äter inte upp varandras marknad, utan vi kompletterar den."*
